summary: This bill terminates all U.S. membership in the United Nations and its organs, agencies, and agreements by repealing the 1945 Participation Act and related laws, closing the U.S. mission, barring all funding and peacekeeping participation, ending diplomatic immunity and use of U.S. facilities, withdrawing from the WHO, and requiring Senate consent plus a withdrawal clause for any future reentry.

scores.thoughts: The bill repeals US participation in the UN and explicitly prohibits any further assessed or voluntary contributions (section 4), while authorizing only minimal funds for termination purposes. This directly reduces federal spending on international organizations.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, or revenue collection.
Repeal of US participation in the WHO (section 7) is included, but the bill does not alter domestic US healthcare systems, coverage models, or public vs. private structures.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration policy, borders, or pathways.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
Section 5 prohibits US participation in UN peacekeeping operations, but the bill does not alter US defense budgets, troop levels, or military spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or protections.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, entitlements, or domestic social spending.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or choice programs.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By terminating UN contributions and related expenditures (section 4), the bill reduces federal outlays, which indirectly supports debt reduction efforts.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related policies.

The bill terminates all US assessed and voluntary contributions to the UN and affiliated bodies (section 4) and ends participation in related agreements, directly reducing this category of international spending.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, unions, or labor policy.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination law.
